solve.official_answer_error: The reason given for (b), '掛け算の 0/1 が出来事で決まる', does not on its own rule out a convolution. B4 replacement atoms are also 0/1 set by events, yet they are proportional (a convolution with h = R·δ) to the event train. The textbook's reasons (§6.4) are different: the effect depends on which year τ falls in, not on the elapsed time t − τ, and two renewals in one year cancel the repair only once, so the effect is not additive. Rubric item (2) should accept either reason.

(b) is also underdetermined. With an annual discrete series, at most one renewal per year and x_t = renewal indicator, y_t = −B·x_t is proportional, i.e. a convolution with h_0 = −B. The answer 'cannot' depends on continuous event times, several renewals per year, or renewal amounts as the input, and the statement specifies none of these, so 'yes, under annual discretisation' is defensible.

solve.missing_knowledge: At the level the rubric asks for, the student can reproduce the answer from 9.5. As a reasoned justification, two proof steps are missing. (i) The 9.5 argument for log10 x uses behaviour as x -> infinity. If log10 x = p/q held only on a small interval, that says nothing about infinity unless the identity is first extended to all of (0, infinity) by the identity theorem for analytic functions. An alternative is that the derivative of a rational function has zero residue at every pole, while 1/x has residue 1. The sqrt argument is complete because it reduces to a polynomial identity. (ii) The step from 'piecewise rational on finitely many pieces' to 'rational on some interval' needs the pieces to be sets defined by inequalities, so that one piece contains an interval. 9.5 leaves this implicit. Both belong in 9.5.

The official answer adds this caveat; the statement should include it. solve.problem_defect: The problem mixes θ_ε with exact node times. θ_ε(T;g) = [g < T(1-ε)] switches at T = g/(1-ε), not at g. So (1), read literally with event nodes at g, fails on (g, g/(1-ε)), and (2) is not exact: the jump is p_g + q_g·g/(1-ε) at T = g/(1-ε), and there is no jump at T = g. Fix: state 'ε→0 (θ = [g<T])' or define the event node as sw(g) = g/(1-ε). Textbook 5.2/5.5 share this imprecision. In (3)(b), the weight e^{-0.03(T-y)} exceeds 1 for the unfinished year y > T (T-y < 0), which is odd for something called a '割引'. The point about T-dependent amplitudes still holds. The 教材 list omits 4.7, where 'amplitudes independent of T' is stated as the premise the answer relies on.

The answer could add a point that settles the matter: adding the refill as a second input (x_5 = m0) still fails (1.431 kg), so the error is time-variance, not just a missing input.

Part (2) 'そのまま比べてよいか' is descriptive but has no rubric. The remark '60 年ちょうどの交換を数えないことで結果が変わっている' is vague: changed relative to what? It means relative to counting the replacement at year 60. Values are correct: 2440 t, 24.4; 2720 t, 22.67 kgCO2e/(m²·年).
solve.problem_defect: Minor: the only expected answer is 'no'. Comparing the two values is legitimate as a sensitivity study of T, though not as a comparison of building performance; the problem does not say which purpose it means.

The textbook's own table defines A4 as 工場から現場への運搬. A4 is counted twice only when the factor also covers delivery to the site (a cradle-to-site, A1–A4 factor).

errors.quote: | (c) 排出ごとに同じ長さの窓 | 各排出から 100 年など | どの時刻でも重み 1 になり、静的な GWP と同じ |
errors.problem: The text uses the research's lettering ((b) and (d) match), but row (c) gives the research's convention (a). The research's (c) is Ventura (2022). In it, each emission's numerator runs over THI, while the CO2 reference pulse runs from t=0 to t_i+THI. The CO2 weight is then R(100)/R(t_i+100). This is less than 1 and falls for later emissions, so it is not static GWP. As written, rows (a) and (c) say the same thing.

errors.fix: Change row (c) to: 各排出を同じ長さ（100 年など）で数えるが、基準の CO2 は t=0 から t_i+100 年まで（Ventura 2022） | CO2 の重みは R(100)/R(t_i+100) で 1 より小さく、遅い排出ほど小さい. Alternatively, drop (c) and keep (a) as the per-emission/static convention, as 18/06 does.

The missing-value propagation rule belongs to the msp engine, not to the model's convention for totals.

errors.quote: （初期の排出 $\alpha$ を年数で割るので、短い期間ほど大きく、長い期間では $\beta/A$ に近づく。$T \to 0$ では限りなく大きくなる）
errors.problem: α is the intercept of the current linear interval, not the initial emissions. It includes every earlier jump and the intercepts of the year-cell kernels, and it can be negative. C/(AT) falls with T only when α > 0. The research says the sign of α decides whether it rises or falls, and T→0 gives +∞ only if C(0+) > 0. When replacements occur, the long-run value is the long-term slope divided by A, for example (b + R/L)/A, not the β/A of one interval.
errors.evidence: 17_WHOLE_BUILDING_TIME_THEORY/03_時間特性の定理と証明.md line 169 (TH-14): 'd SUM05/dT = −α/(AT²) なので、区間の切片 α の符号で増減が決まる。T→0+ で C(0+)>0 なら +∞'. The textbook's own 4.10 gives the long-run per-year value as b + R/L.
errors.fix: Write「α は区間の切片（初期・期末の定数に、それまでの跳びなどが加わったもの）で、α > 0 の区間では T とともに減る。T → 0 では C(0+) > 0 なら限りなく大きくなる。長い期間の極限は区間の β/A ではなく、長期の傾き（例：b + R/L）を A で割った値」.

errors.quote: (c) 按分（端数の交換も割合で数えて $\max(0, T/L - 1)$ 回。(a) 以下になり、$T$ ちょうど交換の直前で差が大きい）
errors.problem: The direction is backwards. The gap (a)−(c) = ⌈T/L⌉ − T/L, for T ≥ L, is 0 at T = nL and near 0 just before. It is close to 1 just after T passes nL. Example with L=15: T=44.9 gives a gap of 0.007; T=45.1 gives 0.993.

errors.quote: | 冷媒の交換の時期 | 交換は年の終わりに行い、翌年の初めに満タン | 漏洩の年の割り当て |
